title: Federal Bank end-to-end dry run of stages 2-6 (first lender) - method test, NO verdict, practice card not on the scoreboard
body: PRACTICE run (L9, L21) of the stock-selection machine on an Indian private bank to find what breaks. No buy/sell/watchlist verdict and none should be inferred. Research, not advice. Stage 2: all 9 hard rules PASS in bank form (no RBI divergence above threshold FY24-25; unmodified FY26 audit; May-2026 auditor change = RBI rotation; ratings CARE AA+/IND AA+/CRISIL AAA FD/S&P BBB- first rating; no promoter, AS-18 lending only to the 60.6% subsidiary Fedbank Financial). Graded flags fired: funding concentration (Kerala 58.8% of deposits per Ind-Ra; NR deposits 34.7%; FCNR(B) +239% via the 2026 special window; granular share 85%->81% in a quarter) and fraud value (Rs 207 cr FY26 vs 79 cr). Stage 3: Q2 FY27 SUE +2.91 -> provisional quintile 5 (not a buy reason, L19). Promise tracker on 6 calls: 29 promises, 9 resolved, MCS +0.93 but unusable (no bank peer base, conservative guidance; 3 unacknowledged goalpost changes: C/I ceiling 53.5->55->56%, CASA 36% '3 years' -> 'at some point'). Stage 4: good-but-misleading numbers dominate: retail +18% YoY is +4% ex Rs 9,438 cr FCNR-backed loans; GNPA 1.32% 'decadal low' with Q2 write-offs Rs 498 cr > slippage Rs 420 cr (~1.49% without); PCR 87% partly a buffer funded by Rs 456 cr IT-refund interest (76.6% excl); ROE 13.6% undiluted vs ~10% on book diluted for Blackstone's 27.3 cr warrants at Rs 227. Cost lines (Schedule 16 FY26, Rs cr): staff 3,225 (IBA bipartite applies; next settlement due Nov-2027), other 3,069 incl service charges 1,019 and card networks 510, DICGC ~380 (cross-foots 12 paise per Rs 100 of deposits), rent 354; PSL-shortfall deposits Rs 5,298 cr drag ~6 bps NIM [EST]. Per outlet: deposits Rs 206 cr, CASA 66 cr, opex 4.9 cr, PAT 2.5 cr [EST]. Stage 5 (new bank mode): price Rs 373.5 (20-Nov-2026), P/B 2.24x fully diluted (2.33x undiluted) needs ROE 21.8% forever at CoE 12.5%; implied CoE at today's diluted ROE ~7.3%; base-case IRR 10.0% vs 12% hurdle; P/B 1.63x own 10-yr median (1.38x) and 1.51x mid-size peer median -> HOT. Stage 6 practice card: size 0 (11 open soft flags without a variant view; EV 1.36x vs hurdle 1.76x).

data.purpose: end-to-end dry run #1 on a lender (stages 2-6)

title: Banks: value on P/B vs ROE with dilution first; read the implied cost of equity, not 'RIM value -50%'
body: A lender's revenue/EBIT/FCF/ROIIC are meaningless, so stage 5 needs P/B-ROE. Justified P/B = (ROE-g)/(CoE-g); the ROE the price needs forever = g + P/B x (CoE-g); the CoE the market is using = g + (ROE-g)/P/B. At an Indian 12.5% CoE, a bank at 2.24x diluted book needs ~22% ROE forever (FEDERALBNK, 20-Nov-2026), and the implied CoE at its ~10% diluted ROE is ~7%. As with P/E names (L21), the strict CoE makes the residual-income value look 50% below price; the useful outputs are the implied CoE, the base-case IRR vs the hurdle, and P/B vs its own 10-yr band. Always put pending warrants/QIPs into book and share count first: undiluted P/B and ROE flatter the bank. Tool: tools/valuation/bank.py ('mode': 'bank').

title: Banks: re-derive the 'good' numbers - growth ex special funding windows, GNPA ex write-offs, PCR ex windfall buffers
body: At Federal Bank (Q2 FY27) the headline numbers misled more than the ugly ones (10 vs 6 rows). Checks that should run on every lender: (1) growth ex special funding windows - Rs 9,438 cr loans against FCNR deposits turned +4% core retail growth into +18%; (2) the NPA walk - write-offs Rs 498 cr exceeded fresh slippage Rs 420 cr, so a 'decadal low' GNPA of 1.32% was ~1.49% before write-offs; (3) coverage bought with a windfall - a Rs 456 cr tax-refund interest gain funded a buffer that lifted PCR from 76.6% to 87%; (4) period-end vs average balances - period-end CASA 7.9% above average; (5) ROE on diluted book; (6) rate-cycle NIM (EBLR share x repo move) vs franchise NIM. Rating agencies and companies define credit cost and top-20 concentration differently; copy the definition.

title: Bank cost lines in physical terms: IBA wage settlement, DICGC premium, CRR and PSL-shortfall deposits are dated, public micro-drivers
body: Security-guard depth for a bank: (a) staff cost = headcount x IBA bipartite scale where the settlement applies (Federal Bank's AR cites the Bipartite provisions; staff Rs 3,225 cr FY26 = 21% of income; the next settlement after Oct-2027 is a dated step - at ~17% on ~60% of staff cost it would be ~5% of PAT [EST]); (b) deposit insurance = ~12 paise per Rs 100 of assessable deposits (Rs 380 cr / 0.0012 = Rs 3.2 lakh cr, cross-foots deposits); (c) CRR = NDTL x CRR% idle; (d) PSL-shortfall deposits (RIDF/NABARD/SIDBI) earn far below loan yield - Rs 5,298 cr at FBL ~6 bps NIM [EST]; (e) card-network and outsourcing service charges scale with volumes (Rs 510 cr and Rs 1,019 cr). None of these was asked on six earnings calls.

title: Promise tracker on banks: cover-letter transcripts, bank KPI vocabulary, bps parsing, ceiling-based goalposts and conservative-guidance bias
body: Dry run on FEDERALBNK found: (1) NSE carries only cover letters for many bank transcripts (website copies needed; fetch.py now flags them and takes --local PDF@DATE); (2) v1 had no bank measures and mapped 'net interest margin 3.2%' to finance cost (a false miss) - 20 bank measures added, scored from bank_kpis.py (NSE integrated-filing XBRL + deck KPIs) because screener's bank page lacks NIM/CASA/credit cost; (3) a pre-existing parser bug read '18-20%' as -20% (affected SKIPPER pending targets); (4) goalpost logic compared floors, missing a raised ceiling on lower-is-better metrics (C/I 53.5->55->56%) and 'by FY28' -> 'at some point'; (5) pending originals were pre-judged moved-goalpost; (6) bank guidance is conservative (NIM guided -5-10 bps, delivered +12), so MCS +0.93 rewards sandbagging: add a guidance-bias metric and a bank peer base before using it (L18); (7) management cited 'guidance we gave' that is in no earlier transcript - date promises from the first traceable statement.

title: Stage 2 for lenders: run disqualifiers v2 in bank form (divergence note, AS-18 connected lending, frauds note, CET1/leverage, funding concentration, quarter-end vs average)
body: v2 hard rules are written for operating companies (fake cash, debtor days). For a bank the same intent maps to: H1a audited cash/RBI balances and investment marks; H1b NIM/RoA/C-I inside the peer band with one-offs traced to external documents; H2 rotation vs resignation (RBI mandates rotation); H5 AS-18 connected lending; exit triggers = the AR 'Divergence in asset classification and provisioning' note, restatement, late results; graded = funding concentration (state, NRI, top-20 depositors, bulk share), fraud-note trend, solvency (CET1 vs floor, leverage ratio, LCR, CD ratio). Use BSE as well as NSE Reg-30 lists (BSE showed a GST order the NSE description hid). Federal Bank: 9/9 hard pass, 2 graded flags fired.

title: PEAD on banks: reported EPS mixes treasury gains, provision buffers and subsidiary profits - check SUE on core earnings before acting on a quintile
body: Federal Bank's SUE path (Q2 FY26 -1.11 quintile 1 -> Q2 FY27 +2.91 quintile 5) used reported consolidated EPS, which includes treasury income (Rs 238 cr in Q2 FY27 vs Rs 12-126 cr in prior quarters), one-offs (Rs 456 cr IT-refund interest in Q4 FY26, offset by a buffer provision) and a 60.6%-owned NBFC. The quintile happened to be robust (normalised EPS still a large beat), but for lenders the avoid-leg rule (L19) should be confirmed on (PPOP - normal credit cost) per share before it blocks a card. Untested: whether bank PEAD behaves like the full-sample result.

title: Stage 6 gap: no base-rate class for banks; build Nifty Bank / Bankex 5-yr outcome distributions including failures
body: The decision card had to use the all-sector, survivors-only 2020-25 class (P(>=3x) 44%), which is wrong for a 9x-levered large bank (P(>=3x) model 3%). Stage-1 task: 5-year outcome distributions for listed Indian banks from several start dates (2008, 2013, 2016, 2020), including Yes Bank, Lakshmi Vilas, Dhanlaxmi-type episodes and delistings via merger, split by starting P/B band. Until then, card outside-view notes on banks are uninformative.
